_comment: Shared topography lookup + coarse-organ -> ICD-O-3 C-code crosswalk consulted by site_capture, presentation_router.site_to_group and dual_group_rules, and the output block (Architecture & File System §4C). Labels drawn from the RedCap topography drop-down (RedCap Options/Topography Redcap.md); redcap_code is that file's 3-digit dropdown value (drop the 'C' and the decimal point).

coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 1's Ia4 dual-group rule for 9591 turns on exactly the C42.2-vs-rest distinction, so these four codes are individually addressable below, never lumped as C42.x.
coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Blood, bone marrow and haematopoietic system
Peripheral nerves and autonomic nervous system
Connective, subcutaneous and other soft tissues
Adrenal gland and paraspinal sympathetic chain
Brain, meninges and central nervous system
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group III keys its decision trees to anatomical COMPARTMENT, so this list must be the full C70-C72 set, not three NOS codes. The router picks the tree from the code chosen here and asks no further question, which makes region capture load-bearing for this group in a way it is not for the others. Expanded 2026-09-14 with the Group 3 build. C71.0 has no REDCap topography option (the dropdown jumps 709 to 711) — see docs/TODO.md.
Craniopharyngeal duct and pineal gland -- consulted by the 8000-8005 (NOS) dual-group rule (DT master §6) alongside C70-C72 and C75.1.
coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Craniopharyngeal duct and pineal gland
Nasopharynx
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 4's sinonasal tree (g4_sinonasal) claims this block for the olfactory-neuroblastoma / sinonasal differential (Group 4 build contract §5). Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (ICCC-3 XId) is the dominant paediatric malignancy at this site in older children, so group 11 is listed too.

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Nasal cavity and middle ear
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: C30.0 is the site ICD-O-3.2 itself prints against 9522/3 Olfactory neuroblastoma; C30.1 is 8690's own site (Middle ear paraganglioma). Both are also classic parameningeal sites for embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (group 9).

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Accessory sinuses
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Kadish B/C olfactory neuroblastoma extends into the paranasal sinuses (group 4); the sinuses are also a classic parameningeal rhabdomyosarcoma site (group 9).

coarse_organ_crosswalk.label: Mediastinum
coarse_organ_crosswalk.note: Group 4's sympathoadrenal tree (g4_sympathoadrenal) includes the mediastinum for posterior mediastinal/paraspinal neuroblastoma; an anterior mediastinal mass in a child is more commonly lymphoma (group 2). The compartment alone does not decide, so both groups are listed.

C42.2.label: Spleen
C42.2.note: Spleen is the exception inside the C42.x set: 9591 at C42.2 routes to Group II (IIb4), not Group I (Ia4) — see presentation_router.dual_group_rules['9591'].

C41.0.label: Bones of skull and face and associated joints (excludes mandible)

C41.3.label: Rib, sternum, clavicle and associated joints

C41.4.label: Pelvic bones, sacrum, coccyx and associated joints

C47.9.label: Autonomic nervous system, NOS
C47.9.note: Peripheral nerve and autonomic nervous system. Two families: the sympathetic chain is where neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma arise (ICCC IVa is site-unrestricted, so morphology decides), and nerve sheath tumours are soft tissue sarcomas (IXb2). Lymphoma is NOT coded here — abdominal lymphoma is C48.2 or bowel.

C72.3.label: Optic nerve (optic chiasm, optic tract)
C72.3.note: 9380 (Glioma, NOS) at this site routes to Group III (IIIb) instead of IIId2 — see presentation_router.dual_group_rules['9380'].

C80.9.label: Unknown Primary Site
C80.9.note: Primary unknown — route by morphology (Architecture §6 / Design Spec §3.3); falls to Group XII only when morphology is itself unspecified (8000-8005).

C48.0.label: Retroperitoneum
C48.0.note: Retroperitoneum carries three families in a child: neuroblastoma of the sympathetic chain (IV), soft tissue sarcoma (IX), and lymphoma presenting as a retroperitoneal nodal mass (II).

C48.2.label: Peritoneum, NOS (Peritoneal cavity)
C48.2.note: Peritoneum is where abdominal Burkitt lymphoma is coded when it presents as a mesenteric or peritoneal mass — the commonest abdominal malignancy in a child at UCI. Desmoplastic small round cell tumour (IX) presents here too.

C71.0.note: NO REDCap topography option exists for this code — the `topo_code` dropdown jumps 709 to 711. Verified against ICD coding/RedCap Options/Topography Redcap.md, 2026-09-14. The tool carries C71.0 because Group III keys its decision trees to anatomical compartment and a thalamic diffuse midline glioma lands here. Until the option is added the clerk has no dropdown value to record. See docs/TODO.md.

C11.3.note: Topography Redcap.md line 56 (pick 113) carries ligature damage in its parenthetical synonym list -- "so! palate" for "soft palate". Not reproduced here: the label above is REDCap's wording trimmed of that parenthetical, per Group 4 build contract §7.1. The REDCap source file itself was not edited.

C30.1.label: Middle ear
C30.1._comment: Topography Redcap.md pick 755 (C75.5, Aortic body and other paraganglia) lists "Glomus jugulare" among its synonyms, and ICD-O-3.2 carries "Glomus jugulare tumor, NOS" as a Synonym on 8690/3 Middle ear paraganglioma. So a reported glomus jugulare tumour can plausibly be sited at either C30.1 or C75.5. Recorded, not resolved -- Group 4 build contract §7.1.

C75.5.label: Aortic body and other paraganglia
C75.5._comment: REDCap's label for this pick (755) lists "Glomus jugulare" among its synonyms, and ICD-O-3.2 carries "Glomus jugulare tumor, NOS" as a Synonym on 8690/3 Middle ear paraganglioma (topography C30.1). So a reported glomus jugulare tumour can plausibly be sited at either C75.5 or C30.1. Recorded, not resolved -- Group 4 build contract §7.1.
